claim: Multi-view hand-hygiene recognition paper dated '2021' (86.36% soap / 93.18% dry hands / 95.45% faucet-with-elbow, ~2.2-2.4 s duration error, 67.8% of frames).
problem: Every number is correct, but the year is wrong. The cited article is Journal of Imaging 2020, 6(11), article 120 (published November 2020) - the MDPI anchor in the URL itself is jimaging-06-00120. Nothing on the page supports '2021'. An outcome carrying the wrong year is a misstatement under my brief.
fix: Change year to '2020' and cite https://www.mdpi.com/2313-433X/6/11/120 (or https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34460564/) alongside the PMC link.

claim: Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit: '$249 list (street pricing seen around $399)', source https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/nano-super-developer-kit.md
problem: The cited NVIDIA product page confirms 67 INT8 TOPS and 8GB memory but contains no price at all - the string '249' does not appear anywhere on it. The price is real but is not in the cited source, so as written the number is unsupported by its citation. The '$399 street pricing' figure is also unsourced.
fix: Cite the NVIDIA announcement that states the price: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/jetson-generative-ai-supercomputer/ ('the price is now $249, down from $499'). Drop the $399 figure or label it as an unverified observation with a source.

claim: FTC guidance (Feb 2023, 'Keep your AI claims in check'), cited via https://cdp.cooley.com/ftc-warns-tech-keep-your-ai-claims-in-check-in-new-ai-guidance/
problem: The cited URL returns HTTP 404 and could not be opened, so the legal claim as sourced is unverifiable. The underlying guidance does exist (FTC business blog, 27 Feb 2023), but the brief offers no working citation for it.
fix: Cite the FTC page itself (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/blog/2023/02/keep-your-ai-claims-check) or another law-firm summary URL that actually resolves; re-verify before publishing.

claim: 'N.J.A.C. 8:24-2.1(i) obliges the person in charge to ensure employees clean their hands effectively through routinely monitoring the employees' handwashing.'
problem: The rule text is confirmed verbatim, but the subsection is misnumbered: the handwashing-monitoring duty sits at N.J.A.C. 8:24-2.1(c)3.i, not 8:24-2.1(i). There is no subsection (i) in 8:24-2.1. A wrong pin cite in a compliance-product positioning document is exactly what an inspector or a client's counsel will catch.
fix: Change to 'N.J.A.C. 8:24-2.1(c)3.i' everywhere, including the inspection-log talking point.

claim: Agot AI product: 'Kitchen camera computer vision for order accuracy and line prompts', sourced to the HME Nitro Vision AI press release.
problem: The cited HME release (3 Apr 2025) does confirm the Agot AI acquisition and Nitro Vision AI, but it describes drive-thru/queue visibility (wait times, drive-offs, mobile pick-up zones), not prep-line order-accuracy prompts. The kitchen-order-accuracy description comes from the other source (azrestaurantpartners.com), not from HME.
fix: Either re-describe Agot/HME as drive-thru and queue vision, or keep the kitchen description and cite https://azrestaurantpartners.com/tools/agot-ai.html for it, marked as third-party and not vendor-confirmed.

claim: Market Force finding 'about 16% of quick-service and fast-casual orders have a problem... one chain's annual cost exceeded $26 million', year '2023'.
problem: The 16% and $26M figures are confirmed verbatim, but the page carries no 2023 publication date - it advertises 'The 2022 QSR Results are in!', so the year is unverified and possibly 2022. The brief is otherwise honest that sample size is not disclosed.
fix: Change year to 'n.d. (page references 2022 QSR results)' or add the post date if it can be confirmed.

claim: 'handwashing is consistently the worst-scoring FDA risk factor' (problem summary).
problem: Overstated. The FDA 2010 Trend Analysis Report shows proper handwashing as the lowest-scoring data item among those listed (24% full service, 61% fast food) and the usual weak item within Poor Personal Hygiene, but the page does not establish it as the worst-scoring factor in every facility type or phase (Improper Holding was 45% in full service).
fix: Reword to 'the lowest-scoring practice in FDA's 1998-2008 observations (24% in full-service restaurants) and the usual weak item within the poor-personal-hygiene risk factor'.

claim: N.J.A.C. 8:24-3.3 'bars bare-hand contact with exposed ready-to-eat food and requires utensils, deli tissue or single-use gloves.'
problem: Confirmed, but incomplete in a way that matters for the pitch: 8:24-3.3(a)4 permits bare-hand contact where the establishment keeps written procedures, handwash-facility diagrams and training acknowledgement. Camera/scan logs could feed that documentation set, which the brief misses.
fix: Add the (a)4 documented-procedure exception and note that camera or scan records can support it.
